mainTopic: Backing out of sales before משיכה, and how אונאה (overcharging) is measured: one-sixth of the item or of the money.
overview: The גמרא finishes a story about a man who left his money in someone's house, and רבא rules that saying 'here is the house' does not make a person a watchman at all. It then explains רבי שמעון's view in the משנה. A ברייתא and רבא show when the seller is locked in even without משיכה. רב חסדא then rules that a buyer who paid but did not pull the goods may also back out. A new משנה sets the line for אונאה at one-sixth, with only a short time to complain. It also tells how the merchants of לוד turned down רבי טרפון's one-third rule. רב and שמואל argue whether the sixth is measured against the item or also against the money paid. Proofs from the משנה all end up fitting רב, and a ברייתא that supports שמואל begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: The money left in the house is stolen
steps.stepSummary: The storyteller refuses to sell. The man leaves his coins with him because night is falling. He is told 'here is the house', puts the coins there, and they are stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said: No. He said: Keep these coins as a deposit, since it's getting dark. I said: Here's the house. He put them in the house and they were stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a story already underway. A would-be buyer leaves his money in the storyteller's house, and the money gets stolen. This sets up the court case that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is how the storyteller answered. He did not say 'I'll watch it.' He only said 'here is the house in front of you.' The next step turns on whether those words make him responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit left with someone for safekeeping
Here is the house in front of you

phrases.english: I said to him: No.
He said to me: Let these coins be
as a deposit with you,
for it has grown dark for me.
I said to him: Here is the house in front of you.
He put them in the house, and they were stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facts of the case: the coins were left in the house after the owner only said 'here is the house,' and then they were stolen.

steps.title: רבא rules: 'Here is the house' makes no watchman
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone who only says 'here is the house in front of you' is not even a שומר חנם, so he does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבא. רבא said: Whoever says 'here is the house' is not a paid watchman, and not even an unpaid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: The owner of the money sues, and רבא rules that the homeowner owes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם must pay only if he was careless, which is a low bar. רבא says these words do not even reach that level. The homeowner never took on the job of watching. He only gave permission to use the space.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid watchman (higher responsibility, pays for theft)
An unpaid watchman (pays only for carelessness)

steps.whatToRemember: Just saying 'here is the house, put it there' does not make you any kind of watchman.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a practical rule: giving someone space is not the same as agreeing to guard their item.

phrases.english: He came before Rava.
He said to him: Anyone who says 'Here is the house in front of you'

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר דְּלָא הָוֵי,
phrases.english: it goes without saying that he is not a paid watchman,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם נָמֵי לָא הָוֵי.
phrases.english: but he is not even an unpaid watchman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the court ruling on the story's facts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'here is the house in front of you' creates no watchman status at all, not even שומר חנם.

steps.title: רבינא asks about the מי שפרע curse
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב טבות: weren't the Rabbis telling רבא that the seller should have taken on the curse of מי שפרע?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: But didn't the Rabbis tell רבא that he should have had to accept 'He Who exacted payment'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a report he heard. The Rabbis supposedly said the seller in this story deserved the מי שפרע curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story was being told about backing out of deals. If the Rabbis said this man needed to accept מי שפרע, that would mean he backed out of a real sale. That would conflict with how the story was just told.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse 'He Who exacted payment', said to one who backs out after money was paid

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: וְהָא אֲמַרוּ [לֵיהּ] רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: I said to him: But didn't the Rabbis say to Rava:
phrases.notes: Now רבינא is talking to רב טבות. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: He should have accepted upon himself 'He Who exacted payment'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the accuracy of the story just told.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of the story where no sale happened.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A report says the Rabbis required מי שפרע, which only fits if a sale was made and then backed out of.

steps.title: רב טבות: That never happened
steps.stepSummary: רב טבות rejects the report entirely. No such thing ever occurred.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Those things never happened.
steps.whatsHappening: רב טבות answers simply that the report is false, so the challenge falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not explain the report away. He denies it ever happened. So the story stands as told, with no sale and no backing out.
steps.whatToRemember: The story stands: no sale, no curse, and the homeowner owes nothing for the stolen coins.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לִי: לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: And he said to me: These things never happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by denying its factual basis.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire report about the Rabbis telling רבא this.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The event behind the report never took place.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: When the money-holder has the upper hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה. A ברייתא limits his rule to when both money and produce are with the seller. If the produce is with the buyer, the seller cannot back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: whoever holds the money has the upper hand. A ברייתא adds: only when money and produce are both with the seller. If the produce is with the buyer, the seller cannot back out, because his money is in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי שמעון's view, and brings a ברייתא that explains its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says only the one holding the money can back out, so the seller can back out but the buyer cannot. The ברייתא says this applies only while the produce is still with the seller. Once the produce sits with the buyer, the seller is locked in too.

keyTerms.meaning: To back out of the deal

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁהַכֶּסֶף בְּיָדוֹ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Whoever has the money in his hand —
has the upper hand, etc.
It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon said: When?
When the money and the produce are with the seller.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כֶּסֶף בְּיַד מוֹכֵר וּפֵירוֹת בְּיַד לוֹקֵחַ –
phrases.english: But if the money is with the seller and the produce is with the buyer —
he cannot back out,
because his money is in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁהַכֶּסֶף בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller can back out only while both money and produce are with him. Once the produce is with the buyer, he cannot.

steps.title: Whose hand is the money in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording: the money is with the seller, so how can the ברייתא say the buyer's money is 'in his hand'?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In his hand'?! It's in the seller's hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reason seems to say the buyer has his money. But the buyer already paid it to the seller. So the wording looks wrong.

phrases.english: 'In his hand'?! It is in the seller's hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the reason in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'because his money is in his hand.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer's money was already given to the seller, so it cannot be in the buyer's hand.

steps.title: Read it: the value of his money is with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the reading: the produce, which is what his money is worth, is in the buyer's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because the value of his money is in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rewording the reason so it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer does not hold his coins, but he holds what they bought, the produce. Since he has the goods, the seller cannot back out.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of his money (what his money bought)

phrases.english: Rather: because the value of his money is in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His money in his hand' meant the buyer still had his coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the buyer holds the produce, which is what his money paid for.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say this. If the buyer has the produce, of course the seller can't back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for teaching something too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the produce is with the buyer, he presumably did משיכה, and the sale is fully done. So there seems to be nothing new here.

phrases.english: Obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא's rule needed to be taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the seller cannot back out when the produce is with the buyer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having the produce means משיכה was done, so the sale is obviously complete.

steps.title: רבא: The seller rented the buyer's attic
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the case: the produce sits in the buyer's upper story, which the seller was renting. So no משיכה happened, yet the produce is in the buyer's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where the buyer's upper story was rented to the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the 'obvious' question by describing a special case where no משיכה took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer never pulled the produce. It stayed where the seller kept it. But the place belongs to the buyer, which is why the ברייתא calls it 'with the buyer'.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.confusionAlert: 'Produce with the buyer' here does NOT mean the buyer pulled it. It is still in the seller's rented space, which happens to be the buyer's attic.

phrases.english: Rava said: What are we dealing with here?
For example, where the upper story of the buyer
was rented out to the seller.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer took the produce by משיכה, so the rule is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: No משיכה was done. The produce is in the buyer's attic that the seller rented.

steps.title: Why money works here: the reason for משיכה doesn't apply
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis required משיכה because they feared a seller would not save produce that was already paid for if a fire broke out. Here the produce is in the buyer's own attic, so the buyer himself would save it, and the worry does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the Rabbis require pulling? In case the seller says: 'Your wheat burned in the attic.' Here it's in the buyer's domain, so if a fire breaks out, the buyer himself will work to bring it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, in רבא's case, money alone locks the seller in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, money buys the goods. The Rabbis made משיכה necessary so that the seller would not ignore a fire once the goods were paid for. In the buyer's own attic, the buyer will rush to save them, so the Rabbis' rule does not apply and the payment stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: the act of acquiring movable goods by drawing them in
A protective decree of the Rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: משיכה was required out of fear the seller won't save paid-for goods. Where the buyer himself would save them, money alone ties the seller to the deal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a Rabbinic rule can be limited by its own stated reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Rabbis instituted pulling?
It is a decree, lest he say to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller, speaking to a buyer who already paid.

phrases.english: Your wheat burned in the upper story.
Here, they are in the buyer's domain;
if a fire breaks out by accident,
he himself will make the effort and bring it out.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer. It's his attic, so he'll rescue his own wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא's case is a real חידוש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the reason for the decree does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without משיכה, the seller can always back out.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the goods are in the buyer's own space, the reason for משיכה does not apply, so payment alone binds the seller.

steps.title: A buyer of wine wants his money back
steps.stepSummary: A man paid for wine. He then heard that the household of פרזק the official was going to seize it, so he asked for his money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man paid for wine. Then he heard פרזק the official's people wanted to take it. He said: Give me my money, I don't want the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story that sets up a question: can a buyer back out after paying but before pulling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we talk about a seller backing out. Here it's the buyer, who is afraid of losing the wine. The question is whether משיכה protects the buyer's right to back out too.

phrases.english: A certain man gave money for wine.
In the end he heard that they wanted to take it —
the household of Parzak the official.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַב לִי זוּזַי, לָא בָּעֵינָא חַמְרָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Give me my money; I don't want the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical case about משיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facts of the case: the buyer paid but did not pull the wine, and now wants to cancel.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Pulling works for buyers too
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that just as משיכה is needed before a seller is locked in, it is also needed before a buyer is locked in. So the buyer may back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב חסדא, who said: Just as the Rabbis made pulling the rule for sellers, they made it the rule for buyers too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא decides the wine case in favor of the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the deal is not final without משיכה, neither side is bound yet. The buyer never pulled the wine, so he can cancel and get his money back.
steps.whatToRemember: Without משיכה, a sale of movable goods is not final for either side. The buyer can back out just like the seller.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He came before Rav Chisda, who said to him:
Just as they instituted pulling for sellers,
so they instituted pulling for buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the wine case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule requiring משיכה applies equally to buyers. A buyer who paid but did not pull may back out.

steps.title: The משנה sets the measure of overcharging at one-sixth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that אונאה is four מעה out of the twenty-four מעה in a סלע, which is one-sixth of the purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Overcharging is four silver מעה out of the twenty-four silver מעה in a סלע, which is one-sixth of the purchase.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It tells us how big a price gap counts as אונאה: one-sixth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is worth 24 מעה, and 4 out of 24 is exactly one-sixth. The משנה says 'one-sixth of the purchase,' and the גמרא will soon ask what that sixth is measured against.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying, a price that is off from the market value
A small silver coin; 24 of them make a סלע
The purchase, the item that was bought

phrases.english: MISHNA: Overcharging

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה כֶּסֶף מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה כֶּסֶף לַסֶּלַע
phrases.english: is four silver ma'a out of the twenty-four silver ma'a in a sela,
phrases.notes: "כֶּסֶף" here means a silver מעה coin.

phrases.english: one-sixth of the purchase.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from the laws of משיכה to the size of an overcharge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה is a gap of one-sixth: 4 מעה out of the 24 in a סלע.

steps.title: How long the buyer has to return the item
steps.stepSummary: The buyer may return the item only for as long as it takes to show it to a merchant or a relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when may he return it? Until he has had enough time to show it to a merchant or to his relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a time limit. The buyer can complain only for as long as it takes to have someone who knows prices look at the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the buyer has had a fair chance to check the price and stays quiet, he can no longer complain. A merchant knows the market, and a relative is someone he would naturally ask for advice.

keyTerms.meaning: To return the item or the deal
A merchant or trader who knows market prices

phrases.english: Until when is one allowed to return it?
Until enough time has passed for him to show it
to a merchant or to his relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to the אונאה rule from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer may return the item only within the time it takes to show it to a merchant or relative.

steps.title: רבי טרפון rules that the line is one-third, and the merchants are happy
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון ruled in לוד that אונאה is eight מעה out of twenty-four, one-third, and the merchants of לוד rejoiced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון ruled in לוד: overcharging is eight silver מעה out of the twenty-four silver מעה in a סלע, one-third of the purchase. And the merchants of לוד were happy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story. רבי טרפון set a bigger line for אונאה, one-third instead of one-sixth, and the sellers liked that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a higher line, sellers could charge more before a deal could be challenged. That is why the merchants were happy at first.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled, gave a practical halachic ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon ruled in Lod:
Overcharging is eight silver ma'a
out of the twenty-four silver ma'a in a sela,
one-third of the purchase.
And the merchants of Lod rejoiced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different measure for אונאה from the one in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, אונאה is one-third, eight מעה out of twenty-four.

steps.title: רבי טרפון adds that the buyer has the whole day to back out
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון told the merchants that the buyer may back out all day long.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The whole day one is allowed to back out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון adds the other half of his ruling. The buyer gets the entire day to return the item, not just the short time to show it to someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part is worse for the sellers. They gained a bigger margin, but deals stay open for much longer. That sets up the merchants' reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To back out of the deal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כׇּל הַיּוֹם מוּתָּר לַחְזוֹר
phrases.english: He said to them: The whole day it is permitted to back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם כׇּל הַיּוֹם מוּתָּר לַחְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי טרפון's ruling. It sets a longer time limit than the one in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, the buyer may back out for the whole day.

steps.title: The merchants choose to keep the Sages' rules
steps.stepSummary: The merchants asked רבי טרפון to leave them as they were, and they went back to following the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Let רבי טרפון leave us as we were. And they went back to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The merchants decided the long time to back out cost more than the bigger margin was worth, so they kept the old rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going back to the חכמים means both of their rules: the one-sixth line and the short time limit. To sellers, a deal that can be undone all day is a bigger problem than a smaller margin.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him leave us alone, leave us as we were
The Sages, the majority view in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows the חכמים: אונאה is one-sixth, and the buyer can complain only for the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Let Rabbi Tarfon leave us as we were,
and they went back to the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ יַנִּיחַ לָנוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן בִּמְקוֹמֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the merchants responded to רבי טרפון's two rulings and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The merchants returned to the חכמים' rules: the one-sixth line and the short time limit.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about what the one-sixth is measured against
steps.stepSummary: רב says the sixth is measured against the item. שמואל says it can also be measured against the money paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: רב said, we learned one-sixth of the item. And שמואל said, we also learned one-sixth of the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about the words 'one-sixth of the purchase' in the משנה. Is the sixth counted from the item's real value, or from the price paid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says only the item's true value counts. שמואל says that if the gap is one-sixth of the money paid, that also counts as אונאה. The next steps use numbers to show what this means.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל says 'נמי' (also). He does not throw out רב's way of measuring. He adds a second way, so a sixth of either one counts.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav said: We learned one-sixth of the item.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: שְׁתוּת מָעוֹת נָמֵי שָׁנִינוּ
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: We also learned one-sixth of the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר רַב אָמַר שְׁתוּת מִקָּח שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'שתות למקח' from the משנה in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the sixth is measured against the item's value. שמואל: a sixth of the money paid also counts.

steps.title: Cases where רב and שמואל agree
steps.stepSummary: An item worth 6 sold for 5 or for 7 is אונאה according to everyone, because the gap is one-sixth of the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Worth six, sold for five; worth six, sold for seven: everyone agrees that we follow the item, and it is overcharging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out the dispute with numbers. First it shows the cases where there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the item is worth 6, a gap of 1 is exactly one-sixth of the item. רב agrees because he measures by the item. שמואל agrees too, because he accepts measuring by the item as well.

phrases.english: Worth six, sold for five,
worth six, sold for seven:
everyone agrees
that we follow the item,
phrases.notes: In both cases the gap of 1 is exactly a sixth of the item's value of 6.

phrases.english: and it is overcharging.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁוֵי שִׁיתָּא בְּחַמְשָׁא שָׁוֵי שִׁיתָּא בְּשִׁבְעָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute from step 18 by naming the cases where both agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the gap is one-sixth of the item's value, everyone agrees it is אונאה.

steps.title: The cases where they argue
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about an item worth 5 sold for 6, and an item worth 7 sold for 6.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is: worth five, sold for six; and worth seven, sold for six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two cases where רב and שמואל argue. It is setting up the next two steps, which give each opinion's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the price paid is 6, so a gap of 1 is one-sixth of the money. Measured against the item, though, it is one-fifth (more than a sixth) or one-seventh (less than a sixth).

phrases.english: Where they disagree is
worth five, sold for six,
and worth seven, sold for six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cases of agreement in step 19, this gives the cases of disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is in cases where the gap is a sixth of the money but not a sixth of the item.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling: both cases are overcharging
steps.stepSummary: Since שמואל also measures by the money, both cases (5 sold for 6, and 7 sold for 6) are אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, who said we follow the money: this case and that case are both overcharging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies שמואל's view to the two disputed cases. In both, the gap is one-sixth of the 6 paid, so both are אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל the price of 6 is the measure, and a gap of 1 out of 6 is exactly a sixth. So both cases get the normal אונאה rule: the deal stands and the difference is paid back.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both cases

phrases.english: According to Shmuel, who said
we follow the money,
this case and that case are both overcharging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's ruling on the two cases named in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, both 5-for-6 and 7-for-6 are אונאה.

steps.title: רב's ruling: one case cancels the sale, the other is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: For רב, 5 sold for 6 is more than a sixth of the item, so the sale is cancelled (ביטול מקח). 7 sold for 6 is less than a sixth, so the gap is forgiven (מחילה).
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, who said we follow the item: worth five, sold for six, the sale is cancelled. Worth seven, sold for six, it is forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רב's view to the same two cases. Since he measures only by the item, the two cases come out very differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of 1 on an item worth 5 is one-fifth, more than a sixth, so the whole sale can be undone. A gap of 1 on an item worth 7 is one-seventh, less than a sixth, so it is too small to claim and counts as forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling the sale; the gap is too big for the deal to stand
Forgiving; the gap is too small, so it is assumed the person let it go

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. Less than a sixth: מחילה. Exactly a sixth: אונאה, the money is returned. More than a sixth: ביטול מקח. רב measures only by the item; שמואל lets a sixth of the money count too.

phrases.english: According to Rav, who said
we follow the item:
worth five, sold for six,
it is a cancellation of the sale.
phrases.notes: A gap of 1 on an item worth 5 is a fifth, which is more than a sixth.

phrases.english: Worth seven, sold for six,
it is forgiven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's ruling on the same two cases, in contrast to שמואל's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, 5-for-6 is ביטול מקח and 7-for-6 is מחילה.

steps.title: שמואל: A sixth from either side counts as overcharging
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says מחילה and ביטול מקח only apply when the gap is not a sixth from either side. If it is exactly a sixth from one side, it is אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: When we say a deal is forgiven or cancelled, that is only where the gap is not a sixth from either side. But where it is a sixth from one side, it is אונאה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains why, in his view, both cases (5 sold for 6, and 7 sold for 6) count as אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the gap of 1 is exactly a sixth of the 6 paid, even though it is not a sixth of the item. For שמואל, a sixth measured on either side is enough for regular אונאה, meaning the overcharge is paid back and the sale stands. Only when neither side gives an exact sixth do we go to forgiving or cancelling.

keyTerms.meaning: A sixth from both sides: measured against the item and against the money
A sixth from one side only

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
When we say there is forgiving or cancelling of the sale,
that is where there is no sixth from both sides.
phrases.notes: He means the gap is not exactly a sixth, whether you measure it against the item or against the money.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא שְׁתוּת מִצַּד אֶחָד –
phrases.english: But where there is a sixth from one side,
it is overcharging.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: כִּי אָמְרִינַן מְחִילָה וּבִיטּוּל מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's side, parallel to רב's ruling in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sixth measured from either the item or the money makes it standard אונאה. מחילה and ביטול מקח apply only when neither side gives an exact sixth.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: measure the sixth against the item only. שמואל: a sixth against the item or against the money both count as אונאה.

steps.title: Attempted proof for שמואל from the משנה's four out of twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says אונאה is 4 out of 24, a sixth. The גמרא suggests this means something worth 20 was sold for 24, which is a sixth only when measured against the money. That would support שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: אונאה is four silver מעה out of the twenty-four in a סלע, a sixth of the purchase. Isn't this where he bought something worth 20 for 24? Learn from it that a sixth of the money also counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה to try to prove that the sixth can be measured against the money, as שמואל says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item was worth 20 and sold for 24, the gap of 4 is a fifth of the item, which is more than a sixth. For רב that would cancel the sale. But the משנה calls it plain אונאה, which only works if you measure 4 against the 24 paid, as שמואל does.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading)
A sixth of the money paid

phrases.english: We learned:
Overcharging is four silver coins
out of the twenty-four silver coins in a sela,
a sixth of the purchase.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי עֶשְׂרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבְּעָה,
phrases.english: Is it not where he bought something worth twenty for twenty-four?
And learn from it:
we learned a sixth of the money too!
phrases.notes: Four out of 20 is a fifth of the item. It is only a sixth when you measure it against the 24 paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הָאוֹנָאָה אַרְבָּעָה כֶּסֶף מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה כֶּסֶף לַסֶּלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רב/שמואל dispute against the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a sixth of the money also counts as אונאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'האונאה ארבעה כסף מעשרים וארבעה כסף לסלע, שתות למקח', read as an item worth 20 sold for 24.

steps.title: Rejection: The case is something worth 24 sold for 20
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה could mean something worth 24 sold for 20. Then 4 is a sixth of the item, which fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he sold something worth twenty-four for twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the משנה's case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item is worth 24, a gap of 4 is exactly a sixth of the item. That is a sixth by רב's measure, so the משנה is no proof for שמואל.

phrases.english: No,
it is where he sold something worth twenty-four for twenty.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה בְּעֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must be measuring by the money.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's numbers can describe an item worth 24 sold for 20, a sixth of the item.

steps.title: Problem: That makes the seller the cheated one, but the משנה is about the buyer
steps.stepSummary: In a case of 24 sold for 20, the seller was cheated. But the משנה's later part gives a time limit for returning the item, and רב נחמן says that time limit applies only to a buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who was cheated? The seller. But look at the later part of the משנה: Until when may one return it? Long enough to show it to a merchant or a relative. And רב נחמן said: They taught this only about a buyer, but a seller can always back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection: the case of 24 sold for 20 doesn't fit the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling below value means the seller lost out. But the סיפא sets a time limit for returning the item, and רב נחמן says that rule is only about a buyer, since a seller has no time limit. So the משנה must be about a cheated buyer, and the 'sold 24 for 20' reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the later part (of the משנה)

phrases.english: Who was cheated? The seller.
Say the later part:
Until when is it permitted to return the item?
For as long as it takes to show it to a merchant or to his relative.
And Rav Nachman said:
They taught this only about a buyer,
but a seller can always back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is about an item worth 24 sold for 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case has a cheated seller, but the משנה's time limit for returning, per רב נחמן, only applies to a buyer. So the משנה must be about a buyer.

steps.title: Answer: Something worth 24 sold for 28
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the case: something worth 24 sold for 28. The buyer was cheated, and 4 is a sixth of the item, which fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he sold something worth twenty-four for twenty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of the משנה that fits both the buyer issue and רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the buyer overpaid by 4, so the buyer is the cheated one, matching the סיפא. The 4 is exactly a sixth of the item's value of 24, so רב's measure works, and the משנה still proves nothing for שמואל.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he sold
something worth twenty-four for twenty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה בְּעֶשְׂרִין וּתְמָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26 with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case was 24 sold for 20 (seller cheated) or 20 sold for 24 (supporting שמואל).
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about something worth 24 sold for 28: the buyer is cheated by a sixth of the item, which fits רב.
steps.whatToRemember: The '4 out of 24' משנה can be read as 24 sold for 28, so it does not prove שמואל's view.

steps.title: New attempted proof for שמואל from רבי טרפון's one-third
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון ruled that אונאה is 8 out of 24, a third. The גמרא suggests this means something worth 16 sold for 24, which is a third only when measured against the money. That would support שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי טרפון ruled in לוד: אונאה is eight silver מעה out of the twenty-four in a סלע, a third of the purchase. Isn't this where he bought something worth 16 for 24? Learn from it that a third of the money also counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for שמואל, this time from רבי טרפון's ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item was worth 16 and sold for 24, the gap of 8 is half of the item. It is only a third when measured against the 24 paid. So רבי טרפון would be measuring by the money, just like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Lod, the city where רבי טרפון ruled

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Tarfon ruled in Lod:
Overcharging is eight silver coins
out of the twenty-four silver coins in a sela,
a third of the purchase.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי שִׁיתַּסְרֵי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה?
phrases.english: Is it not where he bought something worth sixteen for twenty-four?
And learn from it:
we learned a third of the money too.
phrases.notes: Eight out of 16 would be half the item. It is only a third when measured against the 24 paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned aside, the גמרא brings a second proof built the same way.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the fraction can be measured against the money paid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טרפון's ruling in the משנה: 'האונאה שמונה כסף מעשרים וארבעה כסף לסלע, שליש למקח', read as an item worth 16 sold for 24.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: worth 24 sold for 16
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for שמואל from רבי טרפון. The case could be something worth 24 sold for 16, where 8 is a third of the item, which fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: No: it is a case where he sold something worth 24 for 16.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 28. It says רבי טרפון's 8 out of 24 can be read in a way that fits רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 28, the case was worth 16 and sold for 24, so 8 was a third only when measured against the money. Here the item is worth 24 and sold for 16. Now 8 is a third of the item's real value, which is exactly how רב measures.

phrases.english: No:
where he sold something worth twenty-four for sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה בְּשִׁיתְּסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of רבי טרפון's case proposed in Step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי טרפון's 'third' must be measured against the money.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The numbers 8 out of 24 can also describe an item worth 24 sold for 16. That is a third of the item, which matches רב.

steps.title: But then the seller was cheated, and the time limit is only for a buyer
steps.stepSummary: If the item was sold for less than its worth, the seller is the one cheated. But the סיפא gives a time limit for backing out, and רב נחמן says that limit applies only to a buyer. A seller can always back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who was cheated? The seller. But look at the end of the משנה: he said to them, 'All day long one may back out.' And רב נחמן said: They only taught this about a buyer, but a seller can always back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case it just suggested. It is the same kind of problem we saw in Step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling for 16 something worth 24 hurts the seller. The משנה then gives a time limit, 'all day long.' רב נחמן says that limit is only for a cheated buyer, so the משנה must be talking about a buyer. That means a case where the seller was cheated cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: Who was cheated? The seller.
Say the later part of the mishna:
He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי טרפון, speaking to the merchants of לוד in the משנה.

phrases.english: All day long one may back out.
And Rav Nachman said:
They only taught this about a buyer,
but a seller can always back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'worth 24, sold for 16' case from Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי טרפון's case is worth 24 sold for 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case has a cheated seller. But the משנה's time limit, according to רב נחמן, only fits a cheated buyer.

steps.title: Rather: worth 24 sold for 32
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the case to something worth 24 sold for 32. The buyer was cheated, and 8 is a third of the item, which fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he sold something worth 24 for 32.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by flipping the case to an overcharge. This matches the move it made in Step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the buyer overpaid, so the time limit fits, as רב נחמן requires. The overcharge of 8 is a third of the item's worth of 24. So רבי טרפון's 'third' can still be measured against the item, and the proof for שמואל falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in a corrected version.

steps.whatToRemember: Both of the משנה's numbers, a sixth (4 out of 24) and a third (8 out of 24), can be read as worth 24 and overcharged by 4 or by 8. Read that way, they fit רב, who measures against the item's value.

phrases.english: Rather, where he sold something worth twenty-four
for thirty-two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֵי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה בִּתְלָתִין וּתְרֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 30 by switching to a case where the buyer was overcharged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was an undercharge (worth 24 sold for 16), which has a cheated seller.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is an overcharge (worth 24 sold for 32). The buyer is cheated, and 8 is a third of the item, which is consistent with רב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting שמואל: the cheated party has the upper hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the one who was cheated has the upper hand. In its example, something worth 5 is sold for 6, and the buyer may choose to cancel the sale or get the overcharge back. This supports שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with שמואל: the one who had the cheating put on him has the upper hand. How so? If he sold him something worth 5 for 6, who was cheated? The buyer. So the buyer has the upper hand. If he wants, he can say, 'Give me back my money,' or, 'Give me back what you overcharged me.' If he sold him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל. The ברייתא starts with the case of a cheated buyer, then begins a second case with a cheated seller. That second case continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An overcharge of 1 on a price of 6 is a sixth of the money. Against the item's worth of 5, it would be a fifth. The ברייתא still treats this as ordinary אונאה, where the buyer gets to choose. That fits שמואל, who also counts a sixth of the money.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
The one on whom (the cheating) was put
His hand is on top, meaning he gets to choose

steps.confusionAlert: Don't measure the 1 against the 5. The ברייתא's example works as a sixth only when you measure against the price of 6, and that is exactly why it supports שמואל.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in agreement with Shmuel:
The one on whom it was put
phrases.notes: 'It' means the cheating. The person who got cheated is the one who gets to choose.

phrases.english: has the upper hand.
How so?
If he sold him something worth five for six,
who was cheated? The buyer.
So the buyer has the upper hand.
If he wants, he says: 'Give me back my money,'
or: 'Give me back what you overcharged me.'
If he sold him...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the משנה were turned aside, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a sixth can also be measured against the money paid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: worth 5 sold for 6 is treated as אונאה, and the cheated buyer has the upper hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source in this passage that actually supports שמואל. The משנה-based proofs all ended up fitting רב.
